images.title: Angles on a straight line
images.purpose: Show that a straight angle of 180° splits into 80° and 100°.
images.composition: One horizontal straight line with one ray, centred, and an equation line below.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal straight line in grey #6B7280 with a dot E at its middle. One ray in grey #6B7280 from E rising to the upper right at exactly 80° from the right half of the line, with a teal #0072B2 arc for 80°. A amber #E69F00 arc on the left side between the ray and the left half of the line for 100°. Exactly 1 line, 1 ray, 2 arcs.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
80° and 100° that do not add up to a straight line
images.takeaway: The two angles share a straight line of 180°.
images.description: A straight line with a ray from its middle point making 80° on one side and 100° on the other.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the 80° arc and say what is left of the straight 180°.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture of the angle itself; one clean image carries it.
